I am old now, eighty years, and my strength is not what it was. This small piece of land behind my house, the cassava and cocoyam I plant there with small pepper and vegetable between, it is what feeds me and helps my grandchildren. I cannot buy the chemical fertilizer, it is too costly and my children send small money only when they can, so I use the droppings from my goats and the ash from my cooking fire to put on the soil. The stems I keep from last year's cassava I will plant again as my mother taught me, and my grandson will come to help me clear and heap the soil because my back cannot do it alone anymore.
